task_instance: Given a simulated decision-type user query ('What did we decide about the Q3 marketing budget?') and a simulated set of connected MCP tool prefixes (chat + cloud storage present; email, project tracker, CRM, knowledge base absent), produce the full source-management output SKILL.md calls for: a source status table, a query-type-appropriate source priority/search plan, a scope-disclosure footer, a 'connect more sources' guidance message, and a simulated rate-limit handling note.
evidence: Wrote scenario_input.md describing the simulated tool-detection input (since this runtime cannot enumerate real MCP connectors and the task rules forbid calling any MCP/connector tools). Wrote search_report.md containing: (1) query classified as a 'Decision query'; (2) a Source Status table matching SKILL.md's format with 2 connected / 4 not-connected sources; (3) a search plan built from SKILL.md's verbatim Decision-query priority list, filtered/annotated for which sources are actually connected; (4) a scope-disclosure line per SKILL.md's Source Health reporting requirement; (5) a 'connect more sources' message reproducing SKILL.md's exact template with N and the source list correctly substituted; (6) a simulated 429/rate-limit scenario handled per SKILL.md's 4-step procedure (no immediate retry, continue with other sources, user-facing note using the exact template wording, digest note on partial coverage). Verified by cross-checking every generated section against the corresponding SKILL.md rule/template it was derived from (all matched, substitutions correct, no invented sources beyond the 6 listed in SKILL.md). The whole task was accomplished with only file read/write of text/markdown files, no shell, no code execution, no binaries, and no MCP/connector tool calls, consistent with the office-assistant runtime and the sandbox's safety rules.
